message.content:
I'm building a reusable job-search skill for a candidate hunting REMOTE-friendly roles across Europe (AI/automation engineer, solutions engineer, full-stack, technical PM). I need to know which search patterns actually WORK with the WebSearch and WebFetch tools available in this environment.

Use ONLY the WebSearch and WebFetch tools. Do NOT use curl, wget, python requests, or any bash-based fetching — that is prohibited here. If a domain can't be fetched, just record that fact and move on.

Your job: empirically test ATS (applicant tracking system) search patterns and report what works.

1. Test whether WebSearch honors `site:` operators by running several real queries, e.g.:
   - site:job-boards.greenhouse.io AI engineer remote Europe
   - site:boards.greenhouse.io "forward deployed engineer" remote
   - site:jobs.ashbyhq.com AI solutions engineer remote EMEA
   - site:jobs.lever.co automation engineer remote Europe
   - site:apply.workable.com AI engineer remote Italy
   - site:careers.smartrecruiters.com AI engineer remote
   - site:join.com OR site:jobs.personio.com AI engineer remote
   Record for each: did it return results, were the results actual live job postings (vs. board index pages), and roughly how relevant.

2. Pick 3-4 of the most promising individual posting URLs you found and WebFetch them. Report: does the fetch succeed, and can you reliably extract job title, company, location/remote policy, salary (if present), and whether the posting looks currently open?

3. Test 2-3 non-site: queries too, e.g. `"AI engineer" remote Europe 2026 apply greenhouse` and a plain `AI solutions engineer remote EMEA jobs`, to see how much signal generic search gives vs. site-scoped.

Return a concise, factual report:
- A ranked list of search patterns that WORK, with 1-2 verbatim example queries each that returned good results
- Patterns that FAILED or returned junk (be specific about the failure mode)
- Notes on WebFetch reliability per ATS domain (which parse cleanly into title/company/location/salary)
- Any URL tricks you discovered (e.g. Greenhouse embed URLs, query params for remote filters, sitemap or search endpoints that render as text)

Be empirical — every claim should be backed by a query you actually ran. Aim for ~25 tool calls max.

attachment.content:
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- cowork-plugin-management:cowork-plugin-customizer: Customize a Claude Code plugin for a specific organization's tools and workflows. Use when: customize plugin, set up plugin, configure plugin, tailor plugin, adjust plugin settings, customize plugin connectors, customize plugin skill, tweak plugin, modify plugin configuration.
- cowork-plugin-management:create-cowork-plugin: Guide users through creating a new plugin from scratch in a cowork session. Use when users want to create a plugin, build a plugin, make a new plugin, develop a plugin, scaffold a plugin, start a plugin from scratch, or design a plugin. This skill requires Cowork mode with access to the outputs directory for delivering the final .plugin file.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- cowork-plugin: Create a new Cowork plugin from scratch, or customize an installed plugin for a specific organization. Use when: customize plugin, set up plugin, configure plugin, tailor plugin, adjust plugin settings, customize plugin connectors, customize plugin skill, tweak plugin, modify plugin configuration, create a plugin, build a plugin, make a new plugin, develop a plugin, scaffold a plugin.
- explain-usage: Explain where this session's tokens went, with one simple chart in plain language. Use when: explain usage, explain my usage, where did my tokens go, token usage breakdown, what used the most tokens.
- setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install a matching plugin, try a skill, connect tools. Use when: set up cowork, setup cowork, get started with cowork, cowork onboarding, configure cowork, personalize cowork.
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.

content.text:
Testing complete — 26 tool calls. Here's the empirical report.

## 1. Ranked search patterns that WORK

**#1 — `allowed_domains` param instead of `site:` (highest precision)**
Plain query `AI engineer remote Europe` with `allowed_domains: ["jobs.ashbyhq.com"]` returned 10/10 on-domain live postings, all genuinely remote-Europe (n8n, Reedsy, EverAI, Pragmatike). This is a **hard filter**; `site:` is only a soft ranking signal. Use this as the primary mechanism in the skill.

**#2 — `site:jobs.ashbyhq.com` + role phrase + region** (best ATS for this candidate)
- `site:jobs.ashbyhq.com "forward deployed engineer" remote Europe` → 10/10 live postings, Europe-specific (Cohere UK/Europe, ElevenLabs Europe, Luma EU, Camunda EMEA, Zauber GmbH)
- `site:jobs.ashbyhq.com AI solutions engineer remote EMEA` → 10/10 live postings (Mistral, Camunda, WunderGraph, Omni)

Ashby is the single highest-signal domain: modern AI companies, EMEA-aware titles, zero index-page noise.

**#3 — `site:job-boards.greenhouse.io` (note the hyphenated host)**
- `site:job-boards.greenhouse.io AI engineer remote Europe` → 10/10 individual postings
- `site:job-boards.greenhouse.io "technical product manager" remote Europe` → 9/9 postings

**#4 — `site:job-boards.eu.greenhouse.io`** — undocumented EU data-residency variant, surfaces EU-employer postings the `.com` host misses (JetBrains, Prolific, Clarity AI, saasgroup). Query both hosts.

**#5 — DACH/EU-native boards** (strong for a Europe-focused hunt, low competition)
- `site:jobs.personio.com AI engineer remote Germany` → 8/8 postings. Real host pattern is `<company-slug>.jobs.personio.com/job/<id>`
- `site:join.com OR site:jobs.personio.com AI engineer remote` → both domains returned; join.com gave 7 live EU startup postings

**#6 — `site:jobs.smartrecruiters.com`** → 6/6 individual postings with location in the title string (Mirantis "remote in the EU" across Barcelona/Prague/Poznań).

**#7 — Multi-domain OR** works: `site:jobs.ashbyhq.com OR site:job-boards.greenhouse.io AI automation engineer remote Europe` returned a clean blend of both.

**#8 — `site:jobs.lever.co`** works mechanically but is the noisiest: `site:jobs.lever.co automation engineer remote Europe` was dominated by aggregators (Jobgether) and offshore outsourcers (Smart Working Solutions), plus Wikipedia leakage. Also **snippet locations lie** — a result titled "Integration and Automation Engineer (Remote, Full-Time)" surfaced under a "remote Europe" query but the posting is **India-only**. Always verify location by fetching.

## 2. Patterns that FAILED

| Pattern | Failure mode |
|---|---|
| `site:careers.smartrecruiters.com AI engineer remote` | **Wrong host.** Returned only company board index pages (`?search=product`, `?remoteLocation=true`, `?page=2`) — zero individual postings. Use `jobs.smartrecruiters.com` instead. |
| Generic `AI solutions engineer remote EMEA jobs` | Aggregator SEO farms only — Jobgether (4 of 8 results), Wellfound, remoterocketship, Glassdoor, remote100k. Near-zero direct-apply links. |
| Generic `"AI engineer" remote Europe 2026 apply greenhouse` | Mostly aggregators + ZipRecruiter junk, **but** it did surface the `job-boards.eu.greenhouse.io` host — generic search is useful for *host discovery*, not for finding jobs. |
| `site:` as a trust boundary | Leaks off-domain: the greenhouse FDE query returned Wikipedia and builtin.com; the Workable query returned builtin.com. |
| `boards.greenhouse.io/embed/job_board?for=<co>` | **ROBOTS_DISALLOWED** — surfaces in search, cannot be fetched. |
| Legacy `boards.greenhouse.io/<co>/jobs/<id>` | **302 cross-host redirect** to the company's own site; WebFetch returns the redirect instead of following it → costs 2 calls per posting. |
| `api.lever.co/v0/postings/jobgether?mode=json` | `SERVER_ERROR`. Company-specific, not domain-wide — `api.lever.co/v0/postings/actian?mode=json` worked fine. Very large aggregator boards blow up. |

## 3. WebFetch reliability per ATS domain

| Domain | Parses cleanly? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `jobs.ashbyhq.com` | **Best.** Title, company, location, remote policy, **multi-currency salary bands** | Camunda returned US $157,300–$253,600 / UK £98,800–£162,400 / SG S$195,400–S$293,000 + equity. Only domain that reliably yields salary. |
| `job-boards.greenhouse.io` / `.eu.` | **Good** on live postings | DataDome → title, company, "France - Remote", nuanced remote policy. JetBrains → 10 EU cities + application-form field list. Salary usually absent. |
| `jobs.smartrecruiters.com` | **Good** | Clean title/company/location/remote. Salary absent. |
| `join.com` | **Good** | Clean single-posting parse. Salary absent. |
| `<co>.jobs.personio.com` | **Good** with `?language=en` | Clean parse, confirmed English output. |
| `jobs.lever.co` | **Good structurally** | Correct title/company/location/apply state — this is how you catch the misleading search snippets. |
| `apply.workable.com/<co>/j/<id>` | **BROKEN** | Client-side rendered SPA. Systematically degrades to the company "Current Openings" page with title/location/salary all ABSENT. Reproduced identically on Nillion and Hugging Face. Use the JSON API instead. |

**Two silent-failure traps for the skill to guard against:**

1. **Greenhouse closed postings silently degrade to the board index.** `job-boards.greenhouse.io/ketryx/jobs/4611245008` (search said "AI Engineer (Remote - EU)") returned Ketryx's full 15-role board with **no AI Engineer role in it**. The fetch *succeeds* — nothing signals staleness. Detection rule: if the fetch returns many jobs instead of one, treat the posting as **closed**. Confirmed independently via the Greenhouse JSON API (8 jobs, no AI Engineer).
2. **Personio closed postings hard-404** (`exmox-gmbh.jobs.personio.com/job/2607195`), even though search still indexes them. Cleaner failure than Greenhouse.

Search indexes run stale across every ATS — two Hugging Face postings from search were absent from the live API. Always fetch before presenting a role.

## 4. URL tricks discovered

**Public JSON APIs — the biggest win.** All fetch as text and give structured fields:
- **Greenhouse:** `https://boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/<token>/jobs?content=true` → `absolute_url`, `updated_at`, location strings. Best freshness check.
- **Ashby:** `https://api.ashbyhq.com/posting-api/job-board/<org>?includeCompensation=true` → `isRemote`, `isListed`, `publishedAt`, `compensation`, `shouldDisplayCompensationOnJobPostings`.
- **Lever:** `https://api.lever.co/v0/postings/<co>?mode=json` → title, location, `workplaceType` (Remote/Hybrid) — surfaced "Europe, Remote" entries directly.
- **Workable:** `https://apply.workable.com/api/v1/widget/accounts/<subdomain>?details=true` → **the only way to read Workable**; returns titles, locations, remote flags where the HTML page fails completely.

**Caveat on the APIs:** WebFetch's summarization layer truncates long JSON. Both Cohere and ElevenLabs reported exactly 7 and 10 jobs and *omitted* Forward-Deployed roles that exist and fetch fine as HTML. Don't ask "list all jobs" — ask targeted questions ("list only jobs matching X"), or the skill will silently under-report.

**Other tricks:**
- `?language=en` forces English on Personio (many DACH boards default to German).
- **Strip tracking/embed suffixes from Ashby URLs before fetching:** `?embed=js`, `/application`, `?utm_data=hiring.lat`, `?locationId=<uuid>` all appear in search results. Canonical form is `jobs.ashbyhq.com/<org>/<uuid>`.
- Greenhouse `?gh_jid=<id>` is the param that carries the job ID onto a company's own careers site after the legacy 302 — usable to reconstruct a direct link.
- Greenhouse board index `job-boards.greenhouse.io/<company>` fetches fine as a bulk company-wide listing (no API token needed).

**Recommended skill default:** `allowed_domains: ["jobs.ashbyhq.com", "job-boards.greenhouse.io", "job-boards.eu.greenhouse.io", "jobs.smartrecruiters.com", "join.com", "jobs.personio.com", "jobs.lever.co"]`, then verify each hit via the relevant JSON API before presenting it. Skip Workable HTML and `careers.smartrecruiters.com` entirely.
